notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 21% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve (hip surgery) and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
A.J. Greer is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nico Myatovic has taken his spot beside Sam Colangelo and Tim Washe.
Laurent Brossoit was added to the roster on Nov 3.
Nico Myatovic was added to the roster on Nov 3 and has played beside Sam Colangelo and Tim Washe.

Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-six forward. Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen. That line has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 40:00 together.

Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin. That line has had 63% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 198:37 together.
Matt Tomkins was added to the roster on Oct 24.

story.head: Bouchard’s favorite opponent
paras: The Oilers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Anaheim on Oct 7. The Oilers (11-2-3) lost 4-3 in a shootout to New Jersey on Tuesday, while the Ducks have won two in a row. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Ducks fourth (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Oilers first (tied for second). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Ducks’ record (.500) is about what their chances are worth. The Oilers’ record (.781) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.607), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Ducks hound the puck on the forecheck (5th) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (30th). Anaheim has allowed 3.80 goals a game, the third most in the league. As for the Oilers, they lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest) and have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd). They also get their defensemen shooting (3rd), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Ducks’ not so much. Edmonton has scored 4.12 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams like to hit, especially the Ducks (3rd), so expect plenty of it.

Leo Carlsson (5 G / 17 A / 22 P in 15 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. Cutter Gauthier (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 14 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for sixth in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games and five goals in eight games against Edmonton since 2023-24. Connor McDavid (9 G / 31 A / 40 P in 16 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Anaheim. Leon Draisaitl (13 G / 16 A / 29 P in 16 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, tied for second in the NHL.
Lukáš Dostál (4-4-1 / .872 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Anaheim, and Matt Tomkins (1-0-0 / .964 SV% in 1 GS) for Edmonton.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to send Podkolzin, McDavid and Draisaitl out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Gauthier, Granlund and Sennecke.

items.text: Evan Bouchard has a point in twelve straight games against Anaheim, and 18 points in his last twelve against them.
Connor McDavid has a point in all 16 games this season.

The Ducks are newly without A.J. Greer, and have been without Troy Terry for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
The Oilers have been without Zach Hyman since Oct 26, and have had to make do without Matt Savoie all season.
